chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who takes a thing to the man, then he changes his mind for him, so he makes it to be for someone else. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘There is no problem’.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.يَبْدُو: He changes his mind / it becomes apparent to him

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give a gift or charity intended for one person to someone else instead?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies that the initial acceptance of an item on behalf of another does not constitute a binding transfer of ownership (qabd), allowing the agent to redirect it to a different recipient if it better serves the purpose. This ruling is particularly significant in the context of Zakat distribution, where flexibility is permitted to ensure the funds reach the most deserving candidates, reflecting the pragmatic legal principles of Shia jurisprudence regarding agency and gift-giving.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who takes the thing to the man, then he changes his mind for him, so he makes it to be for someone else. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain persons of his people from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus’ab who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Once something was brought to the Holy prophet and he distributed it among the people of al-Suffah (the platform); but it was not enough and he gave it to special ones among them. The Holy prophet, was afraid of what might the others think. The Holy prophet came to them and said, ‘I before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, apologize to you, O people of al-Suffah. Something was brought to us and we wanted to distribute it among you but it was not enough; so we gave it to special ones among you for fear of their impatience and dismay.’”
